decisions.executionNote: Begin a continuous elbow-up approach with the left arm; mallet lies in the left workspace with its head pointing right and toward the robot.
Move above the mallet handle while rotating the open left gripper to align across its shaft; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Complete the shaft-aligned top-down approach, stopping above the handle before descending to grasp.
Descend cautiously toward the handle and correct lateral alignment using the wrist view; gripper remains open.
Refine the downward tool axis and center the shaft in the open jaws before closing; make only a shallow final descent.
Close the left gripper on the visually centered handle after an 8 mm final descent; retention will be checked during a lift.
Lift the closed left gripper 6 cm and inspect whether the mallet rises with it before moving toward the keys.
Mallet appears retained. Raise slightly and turn its head forward-right while moving left, keeping the left wrist in its own workspace.
Raise for clearance and finish positioning the mallet tip over the leftmost red key; estimate the tip offset from the head view before striking.
Lower toward the center of the first red key, correcting the forward alignment while keeping the shaft clamped.
Complete the first red-key downstroke with a small rightward centering correction, then reassess before lifting.
Lift 5 cm after the red-key contact, then advance one key to the right while holding the mallet closed.
Strike the second, orange key with a controlled vertical downstroke, retaining the same mallet orientation.
Lift more than 2.5 cm after the orange-key strike, then move over the third, yellow key without dragging across adjacent keys.
Strike the third yellow key vertically, keeping the left wrist and elbow in the continuous configuration.
Lift clear of the yellow key by 5.2 cm, then advance to the fourth green key while keeping the wrist in the left workspace.
Strike the fourth green key with a vertical downstroke, keeping the mallet clamped and wrist left of center.
Lift 5.2 cm after the fourth key and advance to the fifth cyan key, keeping the left wrist on the left side.
Strike the fifth cyan key vertically with the retained mallet, maintaining configuration continuity.
Lift 5.2 cm after the cyan-key strike, then advance to the sixth blue key while preserving the left-arm configuration.
Center the tip slightly right and strike the sixth blue key with a controlled vertical stroke.
Lift 5.2 cm after the sixth key, then move to the seventh purple key with the left wrist still left of center.
Strike the seventh purple key, with a small centering adjustment while still above it.
Lift clear after the seventh key, then align over the eighth magenta key with a slight mallet turn, keeping the left wrist left of center.
Strike the eighth, rightmost magenta key vertically, then prepare the required final lift.
Lift the mallet 5.2 cm after the final key strike, then retract slightly left while maintaining the grip and clearance.
